item.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.41150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Hasegawa, Takuya Matsumoto, Akito Takashima

item.title: Composition factor algebras and finite representation type
item.description: arXiv:2610.41527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An Artin algebra is called a composition factor algebra if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. We prove that every composition factor algebra is representation-finite. This settles a conjecture of Auslander, Reiten and Smal\o. We also give criteria for comma categories and factorization categories to be of finite representation type.
item.dc:creator: Bo Le, Bin Zhu

item.title: Push forwards of smooth measures on the unitary group in odd characteristic under the Chevalley map are almost bounded
item.description: arXiv:2610.41630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study analytic properties of the Chevalley map $p:\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{c}$ where $\mathfrak{u}$ is the Lie algebra of a unitary group over a local field of odd characteristics. This map essentially sends a matrix to its characteristic polynomial. Our main result is that smooth compactly supported measures on $\mathfrak{u}$ are pushed by the Chevalley map to measures on $\mathfrak{c}$ with density functions in $L^q(\mathfrak{c})$ for all $q < \infty$. We also provide similar results for the Chevalley map attached to the unitary group. An important consequence is an odd characteristic analogue to results of Harish-Chandra stating the local integrability of the orbital integrals on the unitary group and its Lie algebra. Further possible applications to local integrability of characters of admissible representations of unitary groups over local fields of odd characteristic are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Avraham Aizenbud, Nir Avni, Dmitry Gourevitch, David Kazhdan, Eitan Sayag

item.title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $\tau$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $\tau$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.
item.dc:creator: Ping He, Bo Le

item.title: A note on rational wavefront sets for finite special orthogonal groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.41741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rational wavefront sets of irreducible representations of finite special orthogonal groups over $\mathbb F_q$. We assume that $q$ is odd and that both $q$ and its characteristic are sufficiently large. Using {the second author's} results for full orthogonal groups, we determine the maximal rational wavefront sets and the dimensions of the corresponding generalized Whittaker models. We show that each rational wavefront set is the rational closure of its maximal elements. For unipotent representations, we describe the maximal rational wavefront sets in terms of Lusztig's canonical quotient and their behavior under Alvis--Curtis duality.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Li, Zhicheng Wang

item.title: On unitary representations of $p$-adic $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ of purely bad parity
item.description: arXiv:2610.41742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$ or split $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$ over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We classify the irreducible unitary representations of $G$ of purely bad parity: such a representation is unitary if and only if it is of Arthur type, except for one additional family when $G=\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$. In particular, we confirm the remaining case of Ciubotaru's conjecture for $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$, namely that every unitary unipotent representation with integral infinitesimal parameter is of Arthur type.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Heng Lo

item.title: Derived tame monomial algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Marlon Pimenta Fonseca, Zheng Xin

item.title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.41765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $\pi$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $\pi$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Heng Lo

item.title: Decomposing super unitary representations using Berezin integration
item.description: arXiv:2610.41829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I introduce the notion of a family of super unitary representations depending upon odd parameters as well as the notion of a direct Berezin integral of such representations. I use this to decompose the (left-)regular representation of the super Heisenberg group and of a super Heisenberg-like group into smaller (irreducible) subrepresentations. I compare the obtained subrepresentations to the representations obtained by applying (super) geometric quantization of the coadjoint orbits of the corresponding groups. It turns out that for the super Heisenberg group we need coadjoint orbits with an odd symplectic form in order to describe all subrepresentations found in the decomposition and for the Heisenberg-like super group we even need orbits with a non-homogeneous symplectic form.
item.dc:creator: Gijs M. Tuynman

item.title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
item.description: arXiv:2610.41929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines. We also extend the Gaussent-Littelmann stratification to the parabolic setting, prove the Levi branching rule for LS galleries, and compare the resulting gallery model with Haines' maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks in the parabolic setting.
item.dc:creator: Wenzhuo Wang

item.title: Relative homological algebra of filter modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.42080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over an arbitrary ordered set we consider the class of filter modules, i.e. indicator modules of filters in the ordered set. We show that the induced exact structure of filter modules, the so-called filter exact structure, which has filter modules as relative projective modules, admits an explicit projectivization by the distributive lattice of filters. This allows the reduction of the projective-homological properties of the induced exact structure to the standard homological algebra of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$, the incidence algebra of $k$-representations on the lattice of filters. In the case of finite join-semilattices, we leverage the combinatorial structure of the distributive lattice of filters to determine the standard global dimension of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$. By virtue of projectivization we provide lower and upper bounds for the global dimension of the filter exact structure. Moreover, we call an ordered set filter-tiny if its relative injective modules one-to-one-correspond to the standard injective modules. We exploit relative derived functors to show that filter-tiny ordered sets do not admit relative injective prehulls if the relative global dimension is larger than 1. It is open to which classes of ordered sets $Q$ the filter-tininess condition applies, and what the relative injective modules are in the case of non-filter-tiny ordered sets.
item.dc:creator: Fritz Grimpen

item.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.40777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$. When $\mathbb{B}$ is non-zero, it provides a diagnostic for having a target space with non-normalizable modes. For interfaces between QFTs, similar considerations imply the existence of a non-trivial conserved charge associated with soliton absorption / transmission, which means that the interface cannot fully dissolve / disappear. Similar considerations hold for junctions of QFTs, which in the special case of string worldsheet CFTs translate to junctions of string theories. We illustrate these general considerations with a number of non-geometric 2D $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ Landau-Ginzburg models, as well as their natural lifts to 4D $\mathcal{N} = 1$ Wess-Zumino models.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Chakrabhavi, Babak Haghighat, Jonathan J. Heckman

item.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.40891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Pl\"ucker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin, Igor Makhlin

item.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.41059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.
item.dc:creator: Mani Shayestehfar

item.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
item.description: arXiv:2610.41068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $\Delta_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations. When the linearized endomorphism ring of every object is local, we show that a minimal free presentation, whenever one exists, determines the unique minimal full initial subcategory, up to equivalence. Bass's characterization of perfect rings gives a sufficient condition for the existence of such presentations. In particular, every finite category with no nonidentity endomorphisms, such as a finite poset, contains a unique minimal initial full subcategory. In the poset case, our results recover the minimal initial subposet constructed in [BDL27] and [DL26]. When $\mathcal{C}$ is the free category on a finite quiver, we give an explicit construction of its minimal initial full subcategories, show that every such subcategory arises from this construction, and provide algorithms with time-complexity bounds.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Br\"ustle, Justin Desrochers, Samuel Leblanc

item.title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the transition coefficients $b_{\lambda,\mu}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_\lambda(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_\mu(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $\lambda$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $\lambda$ is a hook shape, when $\lambda$ has two-columns and some more simple cases. We prove that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+n,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, extending work of Alexandersson, and we record a stability property and some reduction principles.
item.dc:creator: Aritra Bhattacharya, Ziyi Dai, Qilin Hou, Edward Tong

item.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.41237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.
item.dc:creator: Kiwamu Watanabe

item.title: Kloosterman Sums and Pl\"ucker Height Zeta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41332v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.
item.dc:creator: Li Cai, Jingsong Chai, Yadi Liu, Mingyu Yang

item.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective. In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective. As an application of our results, we compute the equivariant series of the characteristic quasi-polynomials of root systems.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Uchiumi

item.title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
item.description: arXiv:2610.41555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Haiman conjectured that for every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{\lambda,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings. Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_\mu$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Keith McNulty

item.title: Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.41614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.
item.dc:creator: Weiheng Xia, Xiaolei Zhang

item.title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.41828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $\gamma$ with a $K$-orbit $\kappa$, and $M=\kappa\cap\gamma$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $\gamma$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $\kappa$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Ullah

item.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.42022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.
item.dc:creator: Yassine El Kaouni

item.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.42110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Pl\"{u}cker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space. We also introduce a general method to construct invariant elements in perfectoid Tate--Huber pairs, and use this to prove absolute Banach--Colmez spaces of slope $<1$ have perfectoid projectivizations. As applications, we establish vanishing bounds for Scholze's mod $p$ Jacquet--Langlands functor on parabolic inductions, and also prove its vanishing in the top degree on every infinite-dimensional non-supersingular irreducible representation.
item.dc:creator: Zecheng Yi

item.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
item.description: arXiv:2201.00447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.
item.dc:creator: Chuijia Wang

item.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
item.description: arXiv:2509.00954v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam K. Miller

item.title: Brauer graph algebras are closed under stable equivalence of Morita type
item.description: arXiv:2608.14253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stable equivalences of Brauer graph algebras. We prove that a basic symmetric algebra without semisimple summands which is stably equivalent to a Brauer graph algebra is again a Brauer graph algebra. In particular, Brauer graph algebras are closed up to semisimple summands under stable equivalence of Morita type. As consequences, we reprove the closure under derived equivalence established by Antipov and Zvonareva and obtain a solution of the reconstruction problem posed by Rickard and Rouquier for algebras stably equivalent of Morita type to Brauer graph algebras.
item.dc:creator: Pengyun Chen, Nengqun Li, Yuming Liu, Bohan Xing

item.title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.38954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $\phi$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $\rho$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_\rho$, $\overline{\Delta}_\rho$, $IC_\rho$, and $\delta_\rho$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$, which were conjectured to exist by Hansen. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp!}\pi$, and $i_{b!*}\pi$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $\pi$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $\phi$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus, as conjectured by Hansen and Hamann-Lee. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.
item.dc:creator: Nikolas Castro

item.title: Period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$
item.description: arXiv:2506.20942v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the modular symbol approach, we prove the rationality and period relations for certain critical values of Rankin-Selberg L-functions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$ over any number field that contains a CM field.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Jin, Jian-Shu Li, Dongwen Liu, Binyong Sun

item.title: Irreducible representations of tree automorphism groups into Pontryagin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2508.02367v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let G = Aut(T) be the automorphism group of a regular tree T. We study continuous irreducible representations of G that preserve a continuous strongly nondegenerate sesquilinear form of finite index on a Hilbert space. These are already classified for index 0 (unitary case) and for index 1. We show that there are no more representations for index > 1, which completes the classification.
item.dc:creator: Federico Viola

item.title: Closed Colored Models and Demazure Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2512.05479v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct and study solvable lattice models whose partition functions are Demazure characters. Two types of colored generalizations of the five-vertex model can be defined that are called the open and closed models. States of both models are associated with Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns, or equivalently, semistandard Young tableaux. We characterize the tableaux arising from states of the closed model and prove that they form a Demazure crystal. This is stronger than identifying the partition function as a Demazure character: it requires constructing Kashiwara crystal operators on the states through lattice moves and recoloring. For the open model, Brubaker, Bump, Buciumas, and Gustafsson showed that the states realize (crystal) Demazure atoms. We also give a new, independent proof of their result. Bump and Naprienko considered bosonic models involving a parameter t. In these models, the edges and vertices are constructed by fusion of simpler edge and vertex types. Taking t=0 produces bosonic analogs of the open model. By reversing the fusion order, we construct closed bosonic models and establish their Yang-Baxter equations, yielding a Demazure-Lusztig recursion for the partition functions. At t=0, these models specialize to bosonic analogues of the closed five-vertex model, and we prove that their states form Demazure crystals.
item.dc:creator: Yingzi Yang

item.title: Open WDVV equations and $\bigvee$-systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.14077v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The idea of a $\bigvee$-system was introduced by Veselov in the study of rational solutions of the WDVV equations of associativity. These are algebraic/geometric conditions on the set of covectors that appear in rational solutions to the WDVV equations. Here, this idea is generalized to open WDVV equations, which are an additional set of PDEs originating from open Gromow-Witten Theory. We develop -- for rank-one extensions -- algebraic/geometric conditions on the covectors that supplement the $\bigvee$-system to give rational solutions to the open WDVV equations. Examples, and the relation to superpotentials and to Dubrovin almost-duality, are given.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Proserpio, Ian A. B. Strachan

item.title: A stacky resolution of singularities for orders by Azumaya algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.05137v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a stacky resolution of singularities for certain noncommutative spaces which can be viewed as 'finite noncommutative extensions' of schemes. More precisely, we show that any order over a reduced separated finite type scheme over a field of characteristic zero can be resolved by an Azumaya algebra over a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack by a sequence of stacky blow-ups.
item.dc:creator: Timothy De Deyn

item.title: Bounded Bruhat intervals and affine Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.16894v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dyer (1991) proved that, for each fixed length $k$, only finitely many isomorphism types of Bruhat intervals occur in finite Coxeter groups. In this short paper, we prove that this result holds also for affine Coxeter groups, and moreover that this characterizes the affine groups among all infinite Coxeter groups. We also show that the coefficients of $q$ in the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of a Coxeter group are bounded if and only if the group is finite or affine.
item.dc:creator: Grant T. Barkley, Christian Gaetz
